conditions.title: Conditions for buying real estate
conditions.item_1: ** Up to 40% of your salary may be used to repay the loan. You may borrow up to 80% of the value of the property (=loan-to-value ratio). The loan-to-value ratio is the ratio between the amount borrowed and the value of the property.
conditions.item_2: *** You must be able to pay the remaining 20% + one-off costs associated with the purchase and loan from your own resources. If you want to buy a property, you must already have this amount available.
conditions.item_3: It is advisable to keep a buffer in a savings account (e.g. 3 x monthly salary)

ba_mandatory.name: Legally Required Civil Liability Insurance
ba_mandatory.desc: Civil liability insurance covers material and physical damage caused to third parties in the event your car is involved in an accident. You are required to take out CL insurance as soon as your car goes on public roads.
ba_mandatory.coverage: Physical and material damage to third parties|Physical damage to occupants of your own car|Your own material and physical damage is not covered if you are liable

small_omnium.name: Compulsory CL + Comprehensive Insurance
small_omnium.desc: A comprehensive insurance policy does NOT cover damage to your own car.
small_omnium.coverage: See civil liability insurance|+ damage as a result of fire, theft, glass breakage, collision with wildlife and storm damage

large_omnium.name: Compulsory CL + Full Coverage Insurance
large_omnium.desc: Full coverage includes damage to your own car, even if the accident is your fault.
large_omnium.coverage: See comprehensive insurance|+ also material damage to your own car

general_insurance.title: Insurances

fire.name: Fire Insurance
fire.info: Fire insurance protects the value of your home and contents against, among other things, the consequences of fire, storms, flooding and snow pressure. As a tenant: Not legally required, but often contractually obliged in the rental agreement. As an owner: Not legally required, but may be contractually required when taking out a mortgage.
fire.costs_explanation: Tenant: Option 5/5 = {{tenantOption5}} / Shared flat = {{tenantShared}} / City = {{tenantCityApt}} / House = {{tenantHouse}}. Owner: Flat = {{ownerApt}} / House = {{ownerHouse}}
fire.coverage: Damage due to fire, explosion or implosion|Struck by lightning|Storm and hail damage|Smoke and soot damage|Fuel oil damage|Water damage|Glass breakage|...

family.name: Family Insurance
family.info: This insurance covers (part of) the compensation you have to pay if you cause damage to third parties in your private life. This damage can be of a material, physical or other nature. This insurance is not legally required and not expensive, but it is very useful.
family.coverage: Covers damage caused to third parties in your private life|Everyone who is part of the family

hospitalization.name: Hospitalisation Insurance
hospitalization.info: This insurance reimburses your medical costs associated with hospitalisation via the health insurance fund or the Auxiliary Fund for Health and Disability Insurance. The cost is mainly determined by age and your family situation. It is best to take out this insurance when you are young and healthy.
hospitalization.coverage: Doctors' bills, costs for medical care, costs for examinations, payment for the room, expenses for medicines and medical equipment, both in Belgium and abroad|Outpatient costs before and after admission|Costs for home care after a stay in hospital or the costs of childcare for your children|Costs for the treatment of a number of serious illnesses|Important: conditions depend on the contract!

accident.name: Accident Insurance
accident.info: If you are the victim of an accident, you can receive compensation through physical accident insurance. This is in addition to the reimbursements from your health insurance fund. An accident is a sudden, unexpected event that has an external impact on the body of the person insured.
accident.coverage: Permanent disability or death = payment of a capital or annuity. A capital is a one-off payment of a significant sum. An annuity is a periodic payment, for example monthly, for a certain period or until retirement age.|Temporary disability = an annuity.|The reimbursement of medical costs, including costs for prostheses or transport to hospital, funeral costs ...

general_insurance.more_info: For more information on insurances, visit www.wikifin.be

savings.title: Savings and Investments

checking.name: Current Account
checking.amount: This is the remaining amount that you do not put in a savings account or invest in an investment fund.
checking.info: A current account is used to carry out your daily financial transactions. E.g. your salary is deposited into this account and you use it to pay for the things you buy.

savings.name: Savings Account
savings.amount: You can decide this yourself, but take an amount that is included in the overview of return on savings and investments. It is also advisable to keep a buffer in the savings account for unexpected events, e.g. 3x your (and your partner's) net monthly salary.
savings.return: See overview of return on savings and investments over 20 years
savings.info: A savings account is a bank account where you put money that you do not need immediately. In exchange for trusting the bank with your savings, the bank will pay you compensation: interest. This interest consists of a base interest rate and a loyalty bonus. You can deposit and withdraw money at any time.

investment.name: Investment Fund
investment.amount: You can decide this yourself, but take an amount that is included in the overview of return on savings and investments.
investment.return: See overview of return on savings and investments over 20 years
investment.info: Investment funds bring together the savings of different investors into one big pot that the specialised fund managers then use to invest. The big advantage is that as an investor you immediately have a diversified investment portfolio. Different risk profiles are possible: e.g. conservative (little risk), moderate (medium risk) and aggressive (high risk). Depending on the profile, the fund will invest your money in underlying products such as shares, bonds, real estate, commodities, etc. The selected fund must match your investor profile.

savings.more_info: For more information on savings and investments, visit www.wikifin.be

returns_overview.title: 20-year return overview
returns_overview.footnote: Returns are net returns over 20 years based on a one-time deposit. Neutral profile is applied.
